thread:
sasha: kicking off a small field trial for a customer conversational workload — goal: compare FP8 / GPTQ / AWQ with continuous batching + prefix cache enabled vs our fp32 baseline. running on canary cluster c-phi.
ev an: love it — what metrics are we watching? latency p50/p95, token cost, and "accuracy" (LM perplexity + a prompt-level pass rate we use for NLU tasks).
perf-bot: initial run posted: p50=42ms p95=180ms tokens/second=230 cost/token est - see attached summary link (internal)
maria: quick note: the workload is long-prefix heavy (avg context ~1.5k tokens) so prefix-cache behavior matters a lot.
hao: curious — any regressions expected from AWQ on long prefix? previous lab runs hinted at token-shift artifacts when KV caching + fast kernels interacted.
sasha: yea that was my worry. observed something suspicious in run 3 (AWQ + prefetched cache + contbatch=8): ~1.6% drop in prompt-level pass rate vs fp32, but p95 latency improved ~12%.
ev an: can you paste the diff? small numbers but real customers care about these pass rates.
sasha: pasted logs + eval summary: ```
Model    pass_rate    p95    cost/tok
fp32     0.872        205ms  $0.00045
FP8      0.869        195ms  $0.00038
GPTQ     0.861        188ms  $0.00033
AWQ      0.857        180ms  $0.00030
``` 
Note: AWQ run had prefix_cache=on, cont_batch_window=8, batcher_backpressure=enabled.
maria: interesting. AWQ loss ~1.5 percentage points vs fp32. Did you repro with prefix_cache off?
sasha: yes — turning prefix_cache off restores AWQ to 0.871 pass_rate (within noise). so this points to an interaction between AWQ quantization and the prefix cache.
hao: logs show some repeated token mismatches at KV offsets around 1024-1036, like the cache entries being read with an off-by-one relative to fp32. suspect key alignment rounding in the quantized kernel.
ev an: could be the way AWQ packs kv pairs — compacting may change chunk boundary behavior when we prefetch ranges. any quick mitigations?
sasha: short term: two mitigation paths:
  1) disable prefix_cache for AWQ models (config knob per-model) — restores quality but loses latency wins.
  2) reduce contbatch window from 8 -> 4 which reduces collision surface; pass_rate for AWQ w/contbatch=4+prefix_cache=on => 0.868, p95 up slightly to 185ms but still cheaper than fp32.
perf-bot: reproduced contbatch window experiment across 3 nodes, AWQ pass_rate median=0.869, p95=186ms, cost/tok median $0.00031.
maria: good pragmatic path — config per-model defaults: AWQ -> contbatch=4 + prefix_cache=enabled with strict per-key-hash validation. file an infra ticket to add a per-model cache-validate flag.
h ao: opening infra bug: INFRA-5123 "AWQ prefix cache alignment + contbatch interaction". attach logs and candidate repro script.
sasha: repro curl for internal canary (use canary token): ```
curl -s -X POST https://canary.api.redwood/test-generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CANARY' \
  -d '{"model":"awq-v1","config":{"prefix_cache":true,"cont_batch_window":8},"prompt":"<<long-customer-dialog>>"}'
``` 
ev an: thx. next steps? I can spin a small AB where 10% traffic goes to AWQ with the reduced contbatch window and monitor pass_rate and latency. if pass_rate drop >0.5pp we rollback.
maria: also add an eval-based alert: if model.pass_rate drops >0.5pp vs baseline for 30m, then rollback. link to alert: MON-2345.
sasha: agreed. i'll update model_catalog with per-model runtime defaults (AWQ -> contbatch=4, cache-validate=true) and include note in release notes.
perf-bot: experiment finished: AB 10% AWQ-cont4 prefcache on -> pass_rate diff -0.3pp, p95 -9%, cost -31%. no customer-facing incidents in 24h.
ev an: perfect. assign followups:
  - sasha: PR for model_catalog defaults + release note
  - hao: INFRA-5123 repro + kernel trace
  - maria: add alert + run 48h extended AB
sasha: assigned. will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: note: saved artifact to s3://redwood-canary/fieldtrials/1763185605/ — include when you file infra ticket.
hao: quick addendum — if the kernel fix is non-trivial we should consider an automated guardrail: detect quant-models with prefetched cache enabled and enforce contbatch <= 4 until kernel is fixed.
maria: agreed. will add guard in rollout service.
sasha: ok closing the thread for now, will follow up with PR and infra bug. thanks all.
